learning_outcomes.text: Ability to use basic engineering knowledge required for optimization.
Ability to analyze and design a system and a process under realistic constraints and conditions by learning the basic principles of optimization.
Gaining experience in applying basic principles and methods of optimization to solve chemical engineering problems.
Ability to use linear and non-linear programming methods and analyze the accuracy of optimization methods.
Ability to solve optimization-related problems through individual work within the discipline.

syllabus_topics: Definition of Optimization and Basic Concepts
Development of Models for Optimization and Formulation of Objective Function
Linear Programming Method and Simplex Method
Positive definite, negative definite matrices and Hessian matrix
Unconstrained optimization problem solving for single-variable functions
Unconstrained optimization problem solving for multi-variable functions
Graphic method for solving Linear Optimization problems
Algebraic method for solving Linear Optimization problems
Simplex method for solving Linear Optimization problems
Simplex method for solving Linear Optimization problems
Duality method for solving Linear Optimization problems
bibliography: Thomas F. Edgar, David M. Himmelblau, Leon S. Lasdon, Optimization of Chemical Processes, 2nd Edition, McGraw-Hill Companies, 2001.
Luenberger, D.G., “Linear and Non Linear Programming” 2nd Edition, Springer, 2004.
